summary: Implemented the Edge background sync worker skeleton (LOCAL-EDGE-1.6, EDGE-FR-05, product vision §6.2/§10, SP-01). Added SyncWorker — a hosted BackgroundService that periodically performs outbound-only sync with the Relay, driving the sync-engineer's ISyncEngine (the engine owns cursor/idempotency/ordering decisions; the worker only orchestrates transport + lifecycle). Push builds the next batch from the durable outbox via the engine, sends it through the IRelaySyncClient seam, and marks covered entries sent only after the Relay acks (write-then-ack, EDGE-FR-04). Pull requests inbound batches, applies them idempotently via the engine, skips invalid batches without crashing, and enqueues the resulting delivery acknowledgements for the next push (SYNC-FR-05). Transient failures back off with capped, jittered exponential backoff (SYNC-FR-04); outbox entries are never dropped and never marked FAILED merely for being offline. The worker walks the product-vision §10 lifecycle (STARTING → RECOVERING → STARTED → SYNCING → STOPPING) and exposes State/LastSyncAtUtc/LastErrorAtUtc for observability (NF-09). Added the IRelaySyncClient outbound hook (IsConfigured/PushAsync/PullAsync) with a DisabledRelaySyncClient placeholder until the synchronisation feature supplies the real HTTPS transport, keeping the Edge offline-first and the durable outbox retaining every entry (local-edge §7 #4). Wired into Program.cs as a singleton hosted service with SyncWorkerOptions bound from the Sync section.   Added 7 unit tests (push+flush, transport-failure retention, cursor echo, pull+apply+ack enqueue, invalid-batch skip, offline no-op, lifecycle transitions).
